note: Yoav Segelovich, formerly of Yesh Atid, now runs on its list
desc: Conservative Islamist Arab party. Broke precedent in 2021 by joining a governing coalition, focused on funding for Arab towns. Yoav Segelovich, a former Yesh Atid MK and deputy minister, has joined its list as a technical bloc — the first Jewish figure to run with it, and a deliberate signal to the Zionist opposition.

name: Amcha Yisrael
spread: 0–8 — too new for pollsters to agree; i24 has shown it as high as 8
note: New party — has said it will recommend Netanyahu for PM
desc: Launched 25 August 2026 by a retired IDF brigadier general who commanded the Givati Brigade. Pitches itself as a broader, less sectarian right than Otzma Yehudit or Religious Zionism. Winter has said he will recommend Netanyahu for prime minister, though he has stopped short of ruling out sitting with Eisenkot. Netanyahu has warned publicly that the party splits the right-wing vote.

positions.annex: Right-wing on territory; the party has not published a detailed platform.

cautions.text: Winter has said he will recommend Netanyahu for prime minister. He has not ruled out sitting with Eisenkot — but it would be a considerable surprise.
Winter has said Amcha Yisrael seeks a broad right-wing government with 'Zionist partners', which reads as ruling out reliance on Ra'am — but he has not said so outright.

name: The Reservists
spread: 4 — has only just started clearing the threshold in polls
note: Refuses Shas and UTJ over the draft — which points him away from the right
desc: Yoaz Hendel's party, founded in 2025 out of a post-October 7 movement for reserve soldiers and their families. Ran as Zionist Home with Chili Tropper until the two split in September 2026 — Tropper joined Yashar, Hendel kept the party and merged with Yaron Zelekha's New Economic Party, adding an economic platform to a security one. His refusal to sit with the ultra-Orthodox over the draft makes a Netanyahu-led coalition hard to join, which leaves the change bloc as his likelier home.

positions.annex: Supportive of settlement but has not pushed for formal annexation.
positions.draft: Supports a broader, more equal draft — the party's founding issue is the burden carried by reservists.

refusals.text: Hendel has ruled out sitting with the ultra-Orthodox parties over the draft-exemption fight.
Hendel has ruled out sitting with the ultra-Orthodox parties over the draft-exemption fight.

_why: Dissolved 6 Sep 2026. Chili Tropper left to run with Yashar; Yoaz Hendel kept the party, which merged with the New Economic Party and now polls as The Reservists (see above). No longer a column in Wikipedia's table.
